meta.scope: Ecuador batch 5 — Shrimp/aquaculture depth (now the #1 export), tax administration (SRI), and remaining high-value fiscal/commodity nodes. Final push.

candidates.title: Camarón — producción y exportaciones
candidates.publisher: Cámara Nacional de Acuacultura / BCE / INEC
candidates.description: Statistics of shrimp aquaculture production and exports. Ecuador’s leading export product by value, surpassing oil in recent years. Concentrated in Guayas and other coastal provinces.
candidates.notes: Structural export success story. 2025 exports reached record levels (~USD 8.4 bn), overtaking oil as the single largest export earner. ~225–230k hectares in production; major employment generator (especially female labour). China, EU and US are the main markets.

candidates.title: Sector acuícola / Aquaculture statistics
candidates.publisher: Cámara Nacional de Acuacultura / MAG / BCE
candidates.description: Broader aquaculture sector statistics, dominated by shrimp but also covering other cultured species. Complements the product-level shrimp series.
candidates.notes: Industry association and official statistics track production area, employment, export volumes and values. Guayas accounts for ~60% of shrimp production area.

candidates.title: Servicio de Rentas Internas (SRI) — tax collection
candidates.description: National tax administration. Publishes gross tax collection by type of tax (VAT, income tax, ICE, etc.) and performance against annual targets.
candidates.notes: Primary non-oil revenue-side fiscal statistic. 2025 collection ~USD 21.5 bn (record). VAT is the largest single tax. Critical under dollarization because monetary financing is unavailable.

candidates.title: Impuesto al Valor Agregado (IVA) / Value-added tax
candidates.description: Main consumption tax. Rate and base changes are high-visibility fiscal policy instruments; collection is published monthly by the SRI.
candidates.notes: Largest single tax revenue. Recent rate/base adjustments (including expansion of the taxable base) have been material drivers of collection growth.

candidates.title: Deuda pública / Public debt statistics
candidates.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / BCE
candidates.description: Stock and flow statistics of central-government and public-sector debt (external and domestic). Key sustainability indicator under dollarization.
candidates.notes: Critical fiscal-sustainability node. Continuously monitored because dollarization removes the option of monetary financing of deficits.

candidates.title: Provincia de El Oro — shrimp and coastal production
candidates.description: Coastal province that is the second-largest shrimp-producing area after Guayas. Completes the coastal aquaculture geography.
candidates.notes: ~15% of national shrimp production area. Links the commodity (shrimp) to the provincial production and poverty geography.

candidates.title: Provincia de Esmeraldas — northern coastal contrast
candidates.description: Northern coastal province with elevated poverty and a significant share of shrimp and other coastal production.
candidates.notes: Elevated poverty incidence relative to the highland core. Completes the set of major coastal provinces (Guayas, Manabí, El Oro, Esmeraldas).

candidates.title: Cacao y elaborados — producción y exportaciones
candidates.description: Statistics of cocoa production and exports (beans and elaborates). One of the three leading non-oil traditional export products alongside shrimp and banana.
candidates.notes: Strong recent value growth. Completes the product-level view of the non-oil traditional export triad (shrimp–cocoa–banana).

candidates.title: Banano y plátano — producción y exportaciones
candidates.description: Statistics of banana and plantain production and exports. Long-standing traditional export and a major employer in coastal provinces.
candidates.notes: Classic traditional export. Still a large volume and value line; frequently cited alongside shrimp and cocoa in non-oil export analysis.

candidates.title: Provincia del Guayas — core coastal statistical identity
candidates.description: Largest coastal province, containing Guayaquil and the majority of national shrimp production area. Intermediate-to-higher poverty incidence and the largest absolute poverty mass.
candidates.notes: ~60% of shrimp production area; hosts the main port and commercial economy. Completes the provincial set with the largest economic and demographic weight on the coast.

proposed_edges.basis: Shrimp is the largest single non-oil export product.
Shrimp is now the leading merchandise export by value.
Tax collection is the primary non-oil revenue source of the national budget.
VAT is the largest single tax administered by the SRI.
Cocoa is one of the three leading non-oil traditional exports.
Banana is one of the three leading non-oil traditional exports.
Guayas accounts for the majority of national shrimp production area.
El Oro is the second-largest shrimp-producing province.
